Medium humanoid in the D&D 5e SRD bestiary (challenge rating 2, any non-lawful alignment). Holding a bandit gang together calls for force of character, pitiless shrewdness, and a persuasive tongue, and the bandit captain has all three in abundance.

Besides directing a crew of self-serving grumblers, the pirate captain is the same role at sea, with a vessel to guard and steer. Keeping such a crew obedient means handing out prizes and penalties on a steady schedule.

What a bandit or pirate captain hungers for above loot is a fearsome name. A captive who flatters the captain’s pride can expect kinder treatment than one who ignores it or pretends never to have heard of the captain’s storied past.

brain_profile.architecture: Animated, not minded: INT 3, WIS 6. The zombie has no self, no memory worth the name and no fear — only the necromantic instruction and a shambling appetite. The honest contrast in this batch is with the lich-grade minds of batch A–R: same undead class, opposite cognitive poles (here, the pole is zero). No living brain: necromantic animation drives a preserved body-plan. What looks like behaviour is residue — motor habits, hunger imprint, or a bound command — unless the stat block's INT/WIS show a surviving mind. INT 3 (low band): fragments of habit and appetite only; no abstract thought.
